title: EXP-048 — Hello World Part 2: Two Property Classes With One Save and Recovery
objective: Using only the supported Mongoose Web Client Property Classes runtime Form (IdoPropertyClasses), first re-read FX_UMBase and FX_UM and document their metadata and checkout indications without modification. Establish that FX_ItemBase and FX_Cost are absent through fresh native Class Name queries with a working positive control. Create exactly two property-class records using one New action per record: FX_ItemBase with Data Type String, Length 20, Column Data Type nvarchar and Label String ID FX_sItem; and FX_Cost with Data Type Decimal, Length 18, Decimal Position 2, Default Value 0, Column Data Type decimal and Label String ID FX_sCost. Verify both unsaved definitions together, perform exactly one ordinary toolbar Save for both records, confirm the clean result, close and reopen Property Classes once, and perform one fresh exact-name recovery query per new class. Verify both definitions and their observable properties across the runtime Form lifecycle. Classify successful results as observed same-session UI-level recovery only.

in_scope: Read EXP-043, EXP-044, EXP-047 and EXP-047-R2 for established Property Classes navigation, field configuration, evidence procedures and limitations.
Verify the existing authenticated Web Client, DEM configuration, native IdoPropertyClasses Form identity, clean Save state and available editing context before mutation.

At T1, re-read FX_UMBase and FX_UM using supported native Class Name queries. Capture Class Name, Base Class, available data type and label metadata, domain relationships, Locked By and visible checkout indications for both. Do not modify either record.

Establish the absence of FX_ItemBase and FX_Cost separately using fresh native Filter-in-Place Class Name queries with visible criteria, zero-data-row results and a known-existing positive control. Use the operator-accepted case-insensitive coverage inference from EXP-044 and EXP-047-R2 without entering additional case variants.
Create exactly one FX_ItemBase record through native New, setting only Class Name FX_ItemBase, Data Type String, Length 20, Column Data Type nvarchar and Label String ID FX_sItem.

Create exactly one FX_Cost record through a second native New, setting only Class Name FX_Cost, Data Type Decimal, Length 18, Decimal Position 2, Default Value 0, Column Data Type decimal and Label String ID FX_sCost.
Use supported native controls and selection lists where appropriate. Verify each configured value after entry and before further mutation.
Capture the visible asterisk states and distinguish required-field indicators from unknown override semantics without inventing explanations.
Verify that both intended new rows are simultaneously pending and all configured values are correct before Save.
Invoke exactly one ordinary Property Classes toolbar Save for both records. Capture messages, row indicators, field values, checkout indications and the settled Save state.
After a demonstrably clean Save, close Property Classes exactly once through its native Form-tab control and reopen it exactly once through the supported Web Client Open and Select Form workflow.
Perform exactly one fresh native exact-name recovery query for FX_ItemBase and exactly one for FX_Cost after reopening, clearing retained restrictive criteria before each query.
Compare the recovered definitions with their pre-Save configurations and document any changes in formatting, effective values or visible asterisks.
Preserve FX_UMBase, FX_UM and their checkout states. Qualify any preservation aspect not independently demonstrated.
Capture decisive screenshots, accessibility snapshots, action-count reconciliation and concise evidence summaries under evidence/EXP-048/.
Create or modify only the EXP-048 experiment record and files under evidence/EXP-048/.

Modifying FX_UMBase, FX_UM or any other existing property class.
Creating FX_sItem or FX_sCost string resources.
Creating or editing IDOs, IDO projects, SQL tables, application records, Forms, components or string-resource definitions.
Changing the FX_UMs IDO, the FX_UM or FX_Description property definitions, or the EA and DZ test records.
Assigning either new property class to an IDO property.
Adding Base Class, Domain IDO, Domain Property or Domain List Properties relationships to FX_ItemBase or FX_Cost.
Manual metadata checkout, check-in or other metadata lifecycle operations.
Explicit metadata unloading, FormSync, deployment, configuration changes or schema synchronization.
Independent database durability testing, cross-session recovery, runtime property behavior or cache-eviction testing.
Creating or modifying recipes, AGENTS.md, environment files or other experiment records.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight: evidence/EXP-048/ identifies an authenticated, usable Mongoose Web Client, the current DEM configuration and available editing context, and the native Property Classes runtime Form as IdoPropertyClasses. Save is disabled, no unrelated pending change or unexpected prompt exists, and the vendor Form definition remains untouched. Any editing context not exposed by the native runtime UI is explicitly qualified.

Existing-class baseline: before mutation, fresh read-only native queries retrieve the expected FX_UMBase and FX_UM records. Evidence records FX_UMBase's String, 10, nvarchar and FX_sUM values, and FX_UM's Base Class FX_UMBase, Domain IDO FX_UMs, Domain Property FX_UM and Domain List Properties FX_Description, together with available inherited metadata and checkout indications for both. No change to either existing class occurs.

Collision gate: separate fresh Class Name queries for FX_ItemBase and FX_Cost each return zero existing data records, with criteria placeholders distinguished from records. A known-existing positive control retrieves its expected record. Evidence captures the visible criteria, settled results, identities and count indications. If either absence cannot be established reliably, creation is prohibited.

First new class: before Save, exactly one new FX_ItemBase row visibly contains Class Name FX_ItemBase, Data Type String, Length 20, Column Data Type nvarchar and Label String ID FX_sItem. Native field controls or captured accessibility properties confirm each value. No unrelated field was manually changed.

Second new class: before Save, exactly one new FX_Cost row visibly contains Class Name FX_Cost, Data Type Decimal, Length 18, Decimal Position 2, Default Value 0, Column Data Type decimal and Label String ID FX_sCost. Evidence distinguishes numeric zero from blank or null. Both new records are simultaneously present before Save, and visible asterisks are inventoried without assuming their meaning.

Single shared Save: controller actions and screenshots establish exactly two native New operations followed by exactly one ordinary toolbar Save after both definitions were verified. The settled result contains both intended records with their specified field values, Save disabled, no pending-change indicators, no unexpected error or prompt, and no additional metadata lifecycle action. If the first row was implicitly committed by creating the second, stop and do not count the execution as the authorized shared-Save workflow.

Runtime lifecycle: the clean Property Classes Form closes exactly once through its native tab control without a Save or discard prompt and reopens exactly once through Select Form as IdoPropertyClasses. Captures prove the tab disappeared and then reopened in clean Filter-in-Place mode, without unexpected messages or restrictive retained criteria.

FX_ItemBase recovery: one fresh exact-name query after reopening retrieves exactly one FX_ItemBase data record. Data Type String, Length 20, Column Data Type nvarchar and Label String ID FX_sItem match the pre-Save configuration. Save is disabled, and no unsaved-change indication or unexpected message is present. Formatting and asterisk differences are documented.

FX_Cost recovery: one fresh exact-name query after reopening retrieves exactly one FX_Cost data record. Data Type Decimal, Length 18, Decimal Position 2, Default Value numeric zero, Column Data Type decimal and Label String ID FX_sCost match the pre-Save configuration. Save is disabled, with no unsaved-change indication or unexpected message. Numeric display formatting and asterisk states are recorded.

Preservation and final audit: evidence reconciles the FX_UMBase and FX_UM read-only baselines, available subsequent observations and unchanged worker action history. It reconciles two target absences, two New actions, exactly two new records, one shared Save, one close, one reopen and two distinct recovery queries against screenshots and controller records. The repository inventory identifies EXP-048-owned documentation changes, with any unverified working-tree state disclosed. Successful findings are classified observed only, and untested database durability, cross-session persistence and application of either class to an IDO property are expressly excluded.

initial_instruction: T1 — Read-only preflight, existing-class preservation baseline and collision gates only. Read the relevant EXP-043, EXP-044, EXP-047 and EXP-047-R2 records. Inspect the currently authenticated Web Client and clean native IdoPropertyClasses runtime Form without modifying it. Starting from the inherited state, re-read FX_UMBase and FX_UM separately through supported native Class Name queries, capturing their metadata and visible checkout indications. Then establish that FX_ItemBase and FX_Cost are absent through separate fresh Class Name queries, clearing inherited restrictive criteria and using a working known-existing positive control. Capture decisive screenshots of both zero-row results and the positive control, with a concise evidence summary and explicit UI-level limitations. Use only the exact specified class-name spellings. Stop if either target already exists, if filtering or session liveness is unreliable, or if any unexpected prompt appears. Do not invoke New, Save, close or reopen in T1. Do not modify any Mongoose artifact. Record evidence only under evidence/EXP-048/ and update only the EXP-048 experiment record. Leave the Form open and clean for a separately authorized creation task.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261011-003837-AqH7. Rationale: EXP-043 established the native Property Classes workflow, and EXP-047-R2 demonstrated creation, one ordinary Save and same-session recovery of FX_UM. EXP-047-R2 was blocked at AC-9 because FX_UMBase's checkout indication was not independently reverified after Save or reopen; its successful FX_UM recovery remains observed evidence. The operator's next Hello World Part 2 step introduces a distinct capability: creating two independent property classes before committing both with one toolbar Save. This new experiment tests that two-row workflow without modifying existing classes or requiring additional metadata lifecycle operations. It also includes the operator-requested read-only reinspection of FX_UMBase and FX_UM before mutation, without treating that inspection as a repair or replay of EXP-047-R2. | Operator review: exact-value guard (FX_ItemBase, FX_Cost, FX_sItem, FX_sCost, FX_UMBase, FX_UM) and no-JavaScript policy added. The tutorial's Unload All Global Form Objects step is deliberately excluded (operator call, 2026-10-11: EXP-044 showed the wizard lookup offers a newly saved, checked-out class without an unload; the unload will be requested from the operator only if the FX_Items wizard cannot see the classes). Approved by the operator 2026-10-11 with precondition attestation: logged in, configuration OK, Web Client loaded, no unsaved changes.
